newsitem.title: USA: Clinton offers condolences for Israel's Herzog. [CORRECTED 21:28 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Clinton offers condolences for Israel's Herzog. [CORRECTED 21:28 GMT]

text.p: President Bill Clinton on Thursday offered his "heartfelt condolences" to Israel on the death of its former president, Chaim Herzog, remembering him as a courageous soldier, statesman and scholar.

Herzog, a former ambassador to the United Nations who was Israel's president for a decade until 1993, died on Thursday at age 78 after a long illness. (Corrects to show Herzog was formerly an ambassador to the United Nations and not to the United States.)

In a statement, Clinton said Herzog "not only served the Israeli people with distinction as their president for 10 years, he was a courageous soldier in the liberation of Europe and a distinguished leader in the Israeli armed forces.
"He will long be remembered for his years as a statesman and scholar -- he personified a vibrant, emerging Israel, taking its place in the community of nations," Clinton added.

The Irish-born Herzog crammed into his life at least half a dozen careers. He spent more than 20 years in the military, was a lawyer, represented Israel's Labour party in parliament and wrote many books on Israeli history.
Born on Sept. 17, 1918, in Belfast, where his father was a rabbi, Herzog began his university studies in Britain before the Second World War intervened and he joined the military.

He took part in the 1944 Normandy landings, was with the first troops to cross the Rhine, and became British Field Marshal Bernard Montgomery's personal representative to a high-level conference on displaced Europeans immediately after the war.
